question.problem:
Given the matrix 
$F=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(F).$
question.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(F),$ we reduce the matrix $F$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 0 & 19\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$rd columns from the original matrix are ${f}_{1}$ and ${f}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(F)$ is $\{{f}_{1},{f}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
